newsitem.title: CHINA: China media greets new U.N. chief by slamming U.S..
newsitem.headline: China media greets new U.N. chief by slamming U.S..

text.p: Chinese state media on Monday greeted the next U.N. chief Kofi Annan with praise for his predecessor, calls for African unity and warnings against U.S. attempts to go it alone on the international stage.
Beijing has welcomed the U.N. Security Council's selection of Annan to replace current U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whose reappointment was blocked by a U.S. veto.
Washington's opposition to Boutros-Ghali was an example of U.S. unwillingness to put global interests first, the official Legal Daily said in a commentary.
The United States was harming international interests by refusing to put aside Cold War ideology and accept the new mood of international multilateralism, the newspaper said.

"As soon as the United States felt this kind of U.N. multilateralism was not to its advantage it began unilateralist policies...arousing the shock and dissatisfaction of (the) international community," the Legal Daily said.

The People's Daily newspaper, mouthpiece of China's ruling Communist Party, hailed outgoing U.N. chief Boutros-Ghali as a leader who had worked hard to adapt the United Nations to the post-Cold War world.
"The Chinese government expresses great admiration of Secretary-General Boutros-Ghali's work," it quoted Beijing's ambassador to the United Nations Qin Huasun as saying.
Annan's selection had been a victory for African unity in which China had played an important balancing role, it said.
The 58-year-old Ghanaian undersecretary-general for peace-keeping operations had been one of four African candidates to take over from Egyptian Boutros-Ghali.
As Boutros-Ghali's replacement, Annan should be careful not to serve only U.S. interests, the Yangcheng Evening News said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.

"Boutros-Ghali's replacement as secretary-general is the keeper of the 'global village' and not a puppet in the hands of the United States," said the newspaper, which is based in southern Guangzhou city.
"People hope the new secretary general will uphold justice as Boutros-Ghali did, will act for the whole world family and will absolutely not be at the mercy of wanton U.S. hegemony," it said.
